reply: Dear Consumer, we are sorry you have had to contact us several times about this. We understand you are reporting identity theft and asking us to block information on your credit report that resulted from fraud. Under Section 605B of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. 1681c-2), we can block identified information that resulted from identity theft once we receive the required documents. To proceed, please send us: (1) an identity theft report, such as a report filed with the FTC at IdentityTheft.gov or a police report; (2) proof of your identity, such as a government-issued photo ID and proof of address; (3) a list of each item on your credit report you believe is fraudulent, including the creditor or company name, account number (last four digits are fine), and the date it was opened; and (4) a brief statement that the items did not result from any transaction you made or authorized. Once we receive these, we will review your request, and if it is approved we will block the items and notify the company that furnished the information. We will also let you know the outcome in writing. You may also dispute any inaccurate item directly with us under Section 611 of the FCRA. Please reply with the documents or call us if you have questions. Sincerely, Complaints Team

reply: Dear Consumer, we are sorry for the loss of your father and understand how difficult this is, especially while you are managing payments on your Social Security income. We have reviewed your concern about the loan and the deed of trust in your father's name. Because the borrower has passed away, the loan cannot simply be moved into your name by a phone call or a form. Generally, the estate's personal representative (executor or administrator appointed by the probate court in Mississippi) or a legal heir must provide documents such as the death certificate, proof of authority to act for the estate, and proof of your relationship and ownership interest. Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B, a creditor must evaluate a successor or heir for assumption or continuation of a loan on the same basis as other applicants and may not discriminate because of age, receipt of public assistance income, or disability. Your Social Security income may be counted when assessing your ability to repay, but it cannot be refused for being government benefits.
